reason: E2 directly supports that 0.1 at.% B was added to a BCC RHEA to precipitate borides at grain boundaries and improve cohesion and ductility, supporting premises 1–3. However, there is no cited evidence for the irradiation-sink premise (4) or for the preservation of BCC stability and high-T strength in NbMoTaW (5); these are unsupported by the provided passages.
premises: Boron addition improves grain boundary cohesion in BCC refractory high-entropy alloys
Fine intergranular boride precipitates can form with ~0.1 at.% B in RHEAs
Improved grain boundary cohesion enhances room-temperature ductility
Boride precipitates can act as sinks for irradiation-induced He and defects
BCC phase stability and high-temperature strength are preserved after boron addition
